usage: I want to be a doctor
examples: I am a doctor working at a big hospital.
My sister wants to be a doctor.
nuance: 의사 means a medical doctor, and Koreans politely add 선생님 when speaking to one. The job title alone can sound blunt in direct address.
mistakes: Saying 의사님 instead of the natural 의사 선생님

examples: I am a nurse working at a hospital.
My older sister became a nurse.
nuance: 간호사 is the standard word for a nurse of any gender today. The older gendered word 간호원 sounds outdated and is best avoided.
mistakes: Using the outdated word 간호원 instead of 간호사

usage: I go to the police station
examples: I am a police officer who protects the neighborhood.
An accident happened so the police came.
If you get lost ask a police officer.
nuance: 경찰 can mean the police as an institution or one officer by context. To stress a single person Koreans say 경찰관 instead.
mistakes: Confusing 경찰 with 경찰서, which is the station

usage: I want to be a cook
examples: I am a cook working at a Korean restaurant.
The food the cook made is really delicious.
제 꿈은 유명한 요리사가 되는 거예요.
My dream is to become a famous cook.
nuance: 요리사 means a professional cook or chef who prepares food for a living. A head chef is often called 셰프 in modern restaurants.
mistakes: Confusing 요리사 the cook with 요리 the dish

usage: I want to be a singer
examples: I am a singer who sings songs.
제 동생은 가수가 되고 싶어 해요.
My younger sibling wants to be a singer.
nuance: 가수 is the word for a professional singer who performs for an audience. Casual humming or singing at home is just 노래하다, not being a 가수.
mistakes: Using 가수 for anyone who simply sings a song

examples: I am an actor who appears in dramas.
nuance: 배우 covers both male and female actors in film, drama, and theater. The English loanword 액터 is rarely used in everyday Korean.
mistakes: Adding a gender word, since 배우 already covers all

usage: I want to be an athlete
examples: I am an athlete who practices every day.
That athlete won a gold medal.
My older brother is a famous athlete.
nuance: 운동선수 means a professional or competitive athlete in any sport. For a specific sport Koreans attach the name, like 축구 선수 or 야구 선수.
mistakes: Using 운동선수 for someone who just exercises for fun

usage: I want to be a lawyer
examples: I am a lawyer working at a company.
If a problem arises ask a lawyer.
My older sister became a lawyer.
nuance: 변호사 means a licensed lawyer who represents clients and gives legal advice. A judge is 판사 and a prosecutor is 검사, so do not mix them.
mistakes: Confusing 변호사 with 판사 the judge

examples: I am a reporter working at a newspaper.
The reporter asked the mayor a question.
I want to be a reporter.
nuance: 기자 means a reporter or journalist who gathers and writes the news. The more formal term 기자님 is used when addressing one with respect.
mistakes: Confusing 기자 the reporter with 작가 the author

examples: I am a soldier who protects the country.
My older brother is a soldier now.
그 사람은 군인으로 십 년 일했어요.
That person worked as a soldier for ten years.
nuance: 군인 means a soldier or member of the military in general. In Korea many young men serve as a 군인 during mandatory military service.
mistakes: Saying 군인예요 instead of the correct 군인이에요

examples: I am a farmer who grows vegetables in the countryside.
The farmer goes out to the field early.
nuance: 농부 means a farmer who grows crops or raises animals on the land. The respectful term 농부님 is sometimes used, but 농부 alone is standard.
mistakes: Confusing 농부 the farmer with 농장 the farm

usage: I work at a hair salon
I want to be a hairdresser
examples: I am a hairdresser working at a salon.
nuance: 미용사 means a hairdresser who cuts and styles hair at a salon. The workplace is the 미용실, so keep the worker and the place separate.
mistakes: Confusing 미용사 the worker with 미용실 the salon
